short.lead: The builder for step 2a (#357, the house_rules package and the core module) stopped before changing any code, as it was told to. A hook function is the function that answers one kind of hook event. The step 2 inventory (the list in docs/4-systems/plugin-restructure.md of where each block of hook.py goes) puts three hook functions in the core, the module every install gets. Each of the three calls code that belongs to a part, one of the six feature groups such as the design loop or safe git. Your design for step 2 says the core never imports from a part, so one question decides how these links work. The answer also decides whether a part can be left out in step 10 (#348).
short.hint: Tap a row to see what the builder found.
items: Three core hook functions reach into other parts
scope, which runs on every message you send, adds the design loop's stage note (_loop_scope_note, hook.py:5598) and the prompt timer's waiting note (_waiting_scope_note, hook.py:4209).
inject, which runs at session start, adds the safe git branch and identity notes (_agent_branch_block, hook.py:2193; _agent_identity_block, hook.py:2232).

promptran, which runs after a tool call, updates the prompt timer's waiting record through four functions (_waiting_path, _waiting_key, _waiting_update and _waiting_clock, hook.py:4104-4300) that belong to safe git.
Two small things the builder will fix as part of the move

Three places (hook.py:512, 691 and 868) find files by starting from the folder that holds them. Once that code moves one folder down, into scripts/house_rules/, those three must name the scripts folder directly. Otherwise they would look in the wrong folder.

Some fixed values (constants) sit just outside the line ranges of the code that uses them, such as runnable's five at hook.py:3054-3084. The builder moves each one together with the code that uses it.
Nothing from you; these keep behaviour the same.
How the core gets each part's notes

choices: 1. How does a core hook function get a part's contribution?

The core keeps one list for each of the three hooks (session start, every message, after a tool call). When a part is loaded, it adds its own function to the matching list. The core runs whatever is on the list. A part that isn't installed adds nothing.
This is what makes leaving a part out work in step 10, and the core never imports a part. Each list is written down in docs/4-systems/plugin-restructure.md.
Move the eight called functions (the four named in the first row and the prompt timer's four waiting-record functions), and the code they depend on, into the core
Simplest to build now, but design-loop and safe git code then lives in the core, and step 10 has to move it out again.
Split scope, inject and promptran inside hook.py. Each one becomes a core piece and one piece per part, and hook.py calls them in turn. The end-of-reply hook function is already split this way.
No lists to learn, but hook.py has to name every part, so leaving one out in step 10 means editing hook.py.
In every option the behaviour stays exactly the same and every check must pass.
